extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (primary); patent practitioners and applicants (secondary)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for evaluating whether a patent application satisfies the written description requirement of 35 U.S.C. 112, para. 1, including how to analyze original and amended claims, when new matter is present, and appropriate examiner procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written description separate from enablement
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification must contain a written description of the invention that is a requirement distinct from enablement (35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite case law (e.g., Vas-Cath; Univ. of Rochester; In re Curtis) noting that evidence of enablement is not conclusive of adequate written description; treat the two inquiries separately when examining an application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential goal: demonstrate possession
rubrics_metrics.description: The essential goal of the written description requirement is to clearly convey that the applicant had invented the subject matter claimed (i.e., to show possession).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use authorities (e.g., In re Barker; Capon v. Eshhar) and emphasize public notice: the patent must describe the technology claimed so the public is put in possession of what is claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification must describe claimed invention with all limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant shows possession by describing the claimed invention with all of its limitations using words, structures, figures, diagrams, or formulas that fully set forth the claimed invention (Lockwood).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Possession may be shown by reduction to practice, drawings, structural formulas, or distinguishing identifying characteristics. Lack of description of essential/critical features may render the claim unsupported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy is fact-dependent and varies by invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance with the written description requirement is essentially a fact-based inquiry that will necessarily vary depending on the nature of the invention claimed (Enzo Biochem).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must resolve written description issues case-by-case considering the nature of the technology and the disclosure to persons skilled in the art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original claims: strong presumption of adequacy
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a strong presumption that an adequate written description of the claimed invention is present when the application is filed (In re Wertheim).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejections of original claims for lack of written description should be rare; examiner has initial burden to present reasons or evidence why a skilled artisan would not recognize support in the disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: New or amended claims must be supported by original disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: New or amended claims that introduce elements or limitations not supported in the as-filed disclosure violate the written description requirement (and may be new matter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support may be express, implicit, or inherent; applicant should point out where original disclosure supports amendments (see MPEP §§714.02, 2163.06). Corrections of obvious errors that would be recognized by one skilled in the art do not constitute new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: No in haec verba requirement, but support required
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no requirement that claim language appear verbatim in the specification, but newly added claim limitations must nevertheless be supported by the original specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support can be through express disclosure, implicit or inherent disclosure; beware of adding subject matter beyond what the original disclosure conveys to skilled artisans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim as a whole must be analyzed (claim construction)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each claim, determine what the claim as a whole covers and give it its broadest reasonable interpretation in light of and consistent with the written description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include preamble and transitional language in the analysis; consider whether preamble language is a structural limitation; interpret transitional phrases (comprising, consisting essentially of, consisting of) per case law and MPEP guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate sufficiency of structures, acts, or functions recited
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner should determine if sufficient structures, acts, or functions are recited in each claim to make clear the scope and meaning of the claim, including the weight to be given the preamble.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absence of details for well-established terms is not necessarily basis for rejection; limitations should not be imported into claims from the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review entire application to find support for each element/step
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to determining adequacy, review the entire application (specification, claims, drawings, examples) to understand how applicant provides support for the claimed invention including each element and/or step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether examples, figures, and descriptions collectively convey possession; check claims as filed for support of amendments; examine dependent claims, embodiments, tables, and figures for antecedent and specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional-only descriptions may be insufficient (especially sequences/biomolecules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describing a biomolecule or product solely by its function, without a known correlation between function and structure, normally is not a sufficient identifying characteristic for written description purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functional characteristics without structural identification (e.g., sequence) are likely insufficient; processes that produce a product do not necessarily identify the product for written description purposes (see Deuel, Bell, Eli Lilly).

rubrics_metrics.name: Omission of essential/critical feature undermines support
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim that omits matter disclosed to be essential or critical in the specification does not comply with the written description requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the specification explicitly indicates a narrow understanding or that a feature is essential, broadening claims to omit that feature can be rejected; such omissions may also raise enablement or definiteness issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposits of biological material are not a substitute for written description
rubrics_metrics.description: A deposit of biological material may assist but is not a substitute for a written description of the claimed invention; written description of the deposited material must be as complete as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deposits made under 37 CFR 1.801 et seq. help verification but examination proceeds on written description; later deposits cannot support added matter unless regulatory conditions (e.g., 1.804) are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inherency can supply support if necessarily present and recognized by skilled artisans
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosing a device that inherently performs a function or has a property may permit later amendment to recite that function/theory/advantage without introducing new matter, provided inherency is clear to skilled artisans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To establish inherency, extrinsic evidence must show the missing matter is necessarily present and would be recognized by persons of ordinary skill; mere possibility or probability is insufficient (In re Robertson).

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference allowed but must comply with CFR/MPEP
rubrics_metrics.description: Material properly incorporated by reference is part of the application as filed and may be treated as if repeated in the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow 37 CFR 1.57 and MPEP §608.01(p); replacing incorporated material with actual text is not new matter; consider incorporation when evaluating written description and second-paragraph 112 issues (see MPEP §2181).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner initial burden and applicant response obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner has the initial burden of presenting evidence or reasons why a skilled artisan would not recognize written description support; applicant should point out where the original disclosure supports amendments or claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant points to support and examiner finds disclosure insufficient, examiner must present reasons; rejections should follow a thorough review and be based on substantive law and facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim drafting elements to be mindful of (preamble/transitional/functional language)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preamble language, transitional phrases (comprising/consisting essentially of/consisting of), and functional claim language affect claim scope and written description analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret 'comprising' as open-ended; 'consisting essentially of' is middle-ground and may be treated as 'comprising' absent specification definition; functional language for software may be satisfied by disclosure of functions (Fonar) but examine whether undue experimentation is required to implement.

rubrics_metrics.name: New matter prohibition and permissible amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: The prohibition against introduction of new matter (35 U.S.C. 132 and 251) prevents adding information beyond the originally filed subject matter; rephrasing and correcting obvious errors may be permissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mere rephrasing that preserves meaning is allowed (In re Anderson). Corrections of obvious errors allowed where skilled artisan would recognize existence and correction (In re Odd). Beware of relying on later deposits or foreign priority documents to supply omitted U.S. disclosure unless conditions for incorporation or rules allow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard: disclosure must reasonably convey possession to skilled artisan as of filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: The fundamental factual inquiry is whether the specification conveys with reasonable clarity to those skilled in the art that, as of the filing date, the applicant was in possession of the invention as now claimed (Vas-Cath).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use case law and the totality of disclosure (including examples, figures, sequence listings, deposits, and incorporated material) to determine whether possession is conveyed; this is the ultimate test for written description compliance.
